architecture.approach: CONSTRAINT (owner instruction, Gate 2): the existing token definitions are not overridden or replaced. The @theme block in backoffice/src/index.css and the values it already declares are preserved as they are; tokens are only added where a group or step is missing. The two stale values (--color-error #c81e1e, --color-muted #64707f) are the single exception: they are corrected to the values the majority of copies already use, and both corrections are called out here so they are not mistaken for a rewrite. Design tokens already exist in four disagreeing copies, so this feature collapses them rather than introducing a parallel system. backoffice/src/design-system/tokens.ts becomes the single importable source of truth for TypeScript consumers and the existing @theme block in backoffice/src/index.css becomes its CSS projection for Tailwind 4 utilities. The two files cannot import each other, so a dependency-free Node parity script fails the build whenever they diverge, backed by a literal-lint script that fails on any new hex literal or arbitrary-value colour class under backoffice/src and a locale-parity script for en/ar/fr. Two stale values are corrected to the values the majority of copies already use: --color-error #c81e1e to #dc2626 and --color-muted #64707f to #697586. Existing primitives are modified onto tokens, the seventeen missing primitives are created in backoffice/src/common, and the /design-system page is rebuilt to demonstrate every component and state. web is not touched (CON-303) and its divergent token block is recorded as a follow-up.

dataModel.flowDescription: Nothing is persisted and no server or API is involved. tokens.ts is a static as-const object imported at build time by components and read at run time by the parity script through a dynamic import. index.css is a static stylesheet whose @theme block Tailwind compiles into utilities. The design-system page reads tokens.ts to render the token table and renders each component in each state from static example props. The only mutable state in the whole feature is client-side component state: the Toast queue and the open/closed flag of Dropdown, Popover, Tooltip and ConfirmDialog.

securityConsiderations.description: No third-party UI library is added (CON-308), so the feature introduces no new supply-chain surface; icons stay lucide-react and charts stay recharts. CON-511 through CON-520 are recorded NOT APPLICABLE in spec.md because this feature exposes no API endpoint, parses no input on a server and adds no authentication surface.

CON-517 (XSS) is honoured positively: no new primitive uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and Toast, Tooltip and Badge render text children only, never raw HTML. Accessible roles, focus management and non-colour status indication are the CON-517-adjacent controls this feature does implement.
The locale-parity guard fails the build when a translation key exists in one catalogue only, which prevents a partially localised surface from shipping and keeps CON-304 enforceable in CI.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Seventeen new components all mount on the /design-system route; each is a plain function component with no third-party UI dependency, so the route's bundle grows without adding a library. DatePicker and TimePicker use the platform Intl API rather than shipping a locale data package, which is why FR-010 specifies Intl.

The three guard scripts use only node:fs and node:path, add no install step and read a handful of files, so their CI cost is negligible. Tokens are resolved at build time by Tailwind and at module load by tokens.ts, so consuming a token costs no runtime lookup.

The Toast provider uses a single aria-live region rather than one per toast, avoiding repeated announcements and repeated DOM subtrees; static content stays in server-rendered markup with no client state.

risks.description: RISK-001: UI-1 names Storybook, but the demonstration surface chosen here is the /design-system page.
risks.mitigation: Gate 1 was approved by the owner with this surface confirmed. If Storybook is later required, CON-308 is amended first, only P5 changes, and this spec takes a v2.

risks.description: RISK-003 / R-P2: a parity script that has never failed is not evidence that it works.
risks.mitigation: The script is written in P1 and run against the tree before the two stale values are corrected, so it must fail on them first and only then pass.

risks.description: R-P3: 17 new components across P3 and P4 is a large diff that could be reviewed as an undifferentiated block.
risks.mitigation: P3 and P4 are independently reviewable, and each component lands with its /design-system section in the same phase instead of deferring all documentation to P5.

risks.description: RISK-005 / R-P4: web/src/app/globals.css is a hand-copied @theme block that has already drifted and is being edited in a separate thread on feature/gate-binding.
risks.mitigation: The feature confines itself to backoffice (CON-303), the parity script reads only backoffice, and the divergence is recorded as a follow-up for whichever feature owns web.
